strengths: Principled and elegant formulation: Parameterizing local dynamics via a state-conditioned linear operator allows an exact closed-form matrix exponential solution, eliminating the need for expensive numerical ODE integrators and enabling direct end-to-end training via MMD.

Elimination of OT pre-processing: Bypasses the need to precompute optimal transport couplings (e.g., via Sinkhorn iterations), removing a major computational and memory bottleneck that prevents existing methods from scaling.

Strong empirical performance: Achieves state-of-the-art average performance on standard single-cell trajectory benchmarks (EB, Cite, and Multi), outperforming both recent flow-matching (OT-MFM, OT-CFM) and regularized OT (DeepRUOT) methods.

Biological interpretability: By exploiting the linear projection to PCA space, the model projects the learned local operators back into gene expression space to recover directed gene-gene interaction weights, which are quantitatively validated against the literature-curated TRRUST database.

Support for amortized training and scalability: Effectively demonstrates joint training across disparate datasets within a single model and showcases robust scaling on large cell populations where standard OT methods encounter out-of-memory errors.
weaknesses: Low-dimensional latent space constraint: The model relies heavily on a 5-dimensional linear PCA embedding. Consequently, the reconstructed gene interaction matrix $V_{\text{PCA}} A_\theta V_{\text{PCA}}^\top$ has rank at most 5, fundamentally restricting the complexity and dimensionality of the captured gene regulatory networks across thousands of genes.

Evaluation on synthetically inflated data for scaling: Rather than evaluating scalability on genuine large-scale single-cell atlases (e.g., Tabula Sapiens or Chan Zuckerberg CELLxGENE datasets), the scalability experiment relies on resampling existing datasets with added Gaussian noise.

Limited evaluation scope for gene regulatory network discovery: The TRRUST benchmark only tests sign classification (activating vs. repressing) on 6 top predicted source genes, without comparing edge recovery metrics (AUROC/AUPRC) against dedicated GRN inference baselines (e.g., GRNBoost2, GENIE3) or on established benchmarks like BEELINE.

Local linearity over large time intervals: The single-step analytical decode $\exp(A_\theta \Delta t)z_t$ assumes that the local linear operator $A_\theta$ remains stationary over the interval $\Delta t$. While noted as a limitation, the paper lacks a detailed empirical study analyzing trajectory drift or the breakdown of the locally linear assumption over wider temporal spans.

strengths: The paper is clearly structured and well-written, with intuitive visualizations of the locally linear operator concept and latent space dynamics.
Formulating the local dynamics as a state-conditioned linear ODE allows for an exact closed-form matrix exponential solution, avoiding numerical ODE solver overhead during training and inference.

Bypassing optimal transport (OT) trajectory preprocessing reduces memory overhead during training, demonstrating improved computational scalability over full-batch OT methods on larger resampled populations.

Evaluation on benchmark datasets (EB, Cite, Multi) demonstrates competitive marginal matching performance (Wasserstein distance / EMD in PCA space) compared to existing snapshot interpolation baselines.
weaknesses: Overstated claims regarding Gene Regulatory Network (GRN) discovery: The model operates in a 5-dimensional PCA latent space ($d_z = 5$). Projecting the learned $5 \times 5$ matrix back into gene space via $V_{\text{PCA}} A_\theta V_{\text{PCA}}^\top$ constrains the genome-wide interaction matrix to have rank at most 5. Real biological gene regulatory networks are complex, sparse, and cannot be faithfully captured by a rank-5 matrix spanning thousands of genes.

Inadequate and cherry-picked biological validation: The TRRUST benchmark evaluation only assesses 6 selected source genes (JUN, FOS, YBX1, POU5F1, SOX2, HMGA1) and only performs binary sign classification (activation vs. repression) on pre-existing known edges, rather than true GRN structure discovery (predicting whether an edge exists among all gene pairs). Furthermore, there is no comparison against standard GRN inference baselines (e.g., GENIE3, GRNBoost2, SCODE, or even linear correlation).

Conceptual and technical novelty is limited: The concept of Mechanistic Neural Networks predicting locally linear/decomposed dynamical operators was established in Pervez et al. (2024) and Chen et al. (2025). The core adaptation here consists of applying an MLP to predict an eigendecomposed matrix on 5D PCA latents trained with an MMD loss, which is an incremental architectural variation.

Questionable cross-dataset amortization setup: The authors merge CITE-seq and Multiome datasets directly in PCA space despite both datasets measuring different feature spaces and modalities. Merging distinct modalities in unaligned PCA space without rigorous multimodal integration or batch correction lacks biological and methodological justification.

Dependence on low-dimensional PCA: The entire framework critically relies on reducing data to $d_z = 5$ dimensions. While standard on these specific benchmarks, MMD optimization typically scales poorly to higher-dimensional representations, and the matrix inversion regularizer $\mathcal{L}^{\text{inv}}$ becomes computationally and numerically prohibitive in moderate-to-high latent dimensions.

strengths: The formulation of local dynamics via state-conditioned linear ODEs ($z' = A_\theta(z, t) z$) is mathematically elegant and allows for closed-form analytical integration via matrix exponentials, completely bypassing expensive numerical ODE solvers during training and inference.

Unlike many flow-matching and optimal transport based approaches (e.g., OT-CFM, OT-MFM, DeepRUOT), Cell-MNN eliminates dataset-wide optimal transport preprocessing, substantially improving training scalability with respect to sample size $N$.

Competitive empirical performance: Cell-MNN achieves state-of-the-art average Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) across standard single-cell benchmark datasets (Cite, EB, Multi) and outperforms the OT-Interpolate baseline across all datasets.

The explicit linear operator enables direct projection back to the gene expression space ($V_{PCA} A_\theta V_{PCA}^\top$), providing an interpretable representation of gene regulatory interactions that is validated against the curated TRRUST database.
The paper is well-structured, clearly written, and thoroughly contextualized within the relevant literature on Neural ODEs, flow matching, and mechanistic networks.
weaknesses: A fundamental limitation of the gene regulatory network (GRN) extraction is dimensionality: because the model operates in a $d_z = 5$-dimensional PCA space, the reconstructed gene-gene interaction matrix $V_{PCA} A_\theta V_{PCA}^\top \in \mathbb{R}^{d_x \times d_x}$ has a maximum rank of 5. Representing interactions among thousands of genes using a rank-5 matrix is inherently low-capacity, which limits the biological fidelity and completeness of the inferred network.

The evaluation on the TRRUST database only benchmarks against a naive random guessing baseline and does not compare against established GRN inference methods (e.g., GRNBoost2, GENIE3) or Jacobian-based interaction extraction from Neural ODEs/Flow Matching models.

The mathematical reparameterization $f(z, t) = A(z, t)z$ requires $f(0, t) = 0$, meaning the origin must be an equilibrium / fixed point. Given that PCA centers data at zero, the paper does not sufficiently discuss the biological and dynamical implications of enforcing zero velocity at the empirical mean.

The synthetic inflation experiment in Section 4.3 adds Gaussian noise in the 5D PCA space rather than testing on a truly large, high-throughput scRNA-seq biological dataset with hundreds of thousands of real cells.
